title: Timber volume of black cherry trees
intro:
Real data: 31 black cherry trees felled in the Allegheny National Forest, Pennsylvania (R's trees data set; Ryan, Joiner and Ryan, 1976). For each tree the table gives the diameter (inches, measured 4.5 ft above the ground), the height (ft) and the usable timber volume (cubic feet). A forester wants to estimate the timber in a standing tree from its diameter, which is easy to measure.

Regress volume (y) on diameter (x). Find the slope, R², the residual standard error σ̂, the predicted volume of a tree 15 inches across, and the 95 % prediction interval for that one tree. Give every answer to two decimals.

To use the Workbench: press **Copy the data**, press Ctrl+B, click **+ Data table** and paste (Ctrl+V). Choose **Simple linear regression**, set **x column** to *Diameter (in)*, **y column** to *Volume (cu ft)*, **Confidence level** to 0.95 and **Predict at x₀, optional** to 15. Read **Slope (b₁)**, **R²**, **Residual standard error (σ̂)**, **Fitted y at x₀**, **New observation lower** and **New observation upper**. Ctrl+L brings you back.

Before you write to the forester, look at the residual plot (the second figure in the Workbench). Is it a shapeless band? What would a pattern mean for the interval you give?

Slope.says: That is the slope of volume on height. The forester's predictor is the diameter: set x to the diameter column.

NewLower.says: That is the confidence interval for the mean volume of all 15-inch trees. One tree varies more: use the prediction interval (New observation).

NewUpper.says: That is the confidence interval for the mean volume of all 15-inch trees. One tree varies more: use the prediction interval (New observation).

hints: Volume is y, diameter is x. The height column is not used in this exercise (Module 12 adds it as a second predictor).
b₁ = S_xy / S_xx, b₀ = ȳ − b₁x̄, R² = SS regression / SS total, σ̂ = √(SS error / (n − 2)) with n = 31.

At x₀ = 15: ŷ₀ = b₀ + 15 b₁ ± t(0.025, 29) × σ̂ √(1 + 1/n + (x₀ − x̄)²/S_xx). In R the data are built in, with the diameter called Girth: fit <- lm(Volume ~ Girth, data = trees); predict(fit, data.frame(Girth = 15), interval = "prediction").
